brief: Goldman Sachs credit strategy (Reid Zhou, 8 September 2026) argues credit valuations remain stretched even after recent spread widening, which is why credit screens as an attractive market in which to buy tail hedges, but the desk states that timing a broader widening is uncertain. That uncertainty drives the construction: because entry timing cannot be pinned down, the desk prefers hedges that reduce carry bleed while preserving convexity rather than paying to hold protection. The preferred expression is shorting the cash-synthetic basis, a short ex-hyperscaler cash basket against long CDX IG 10Y, a structure the note says is currently carry positive so it offsets the cost of maintaining downside protection. The supporting case: hyperscaler capex intensity has accelerated over the past two years with capex approaching 30% of revenue, hyperscaler credit has driven the recent spread widening and the hyperscaler versus ex-hyperscaler spread differential has widened materially during 2026 and sits well above its year-to-date average, while the IG 10Y ex-hyperscaler basis sits near the low end of its five-year range and below its historical average, which the note says leaves room for further widening in a broader risk-off scenario.
